name: New York
title: New York Rebate Calculator 2026: NYS Clean Heat, Con Edison, National Grid and More
h1: New York Rebate Calculator 2026: What Your Utility Pays
desc: Free New York rebate calculator. NYS Clean Heat heat pump rebates by utility, heat pump water heaters and free income-based upgrades, with the official source for every amount.
intro: Answer a few questions and see which New York rebates fit your home, with a source for every number.
short: New York's heat pump rebate is NYS Clean Heat, paid through your electric utility: about $5,000 to $7,000 for a full system (more in a disadvantaged community, and up to $10,000 or more with the old system removed). Long Island is separate, through PSEG Long Island. Clean Heat and your utility's rebate are the same money, so they do not stack.
faq: How much is the New York heat pump rebate in 2026?

It depends on your utility. For a single-family full-system replacement, Con Edison pays $7,000, National Grid, NYSEG and RG&E pay $6,000, and Central Hudson and Orange & Rockland pay $5,000. Disadvantaged communities get more. With the old system removed, the top tier reaches $10,000 in several areas. PSEG Long Island pays $4,000 to $7,500.
Does NYS Clean Heat stack with my utility rebate?
No. NYS Clean Heat is the utility rebate. It is run by Central Hudson, Con Edison, National Grid, NYSEG, Orange & Rockland and RG&E, so adding both counts the same money twice.
Is there a limit on how much I can get?
Yes. Clean Heat incentives are capped at 70% of the project cost, or 85% in a disadvantaged community.
What if my income is low?

EmPower+ from NYSERDA gives free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate to income-eligible owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Moderate-income homes get 50% of the cost up to $6,000 or $7,000.

programs.name: Con Edison Clean Heat: full system
programs.rules: Single-family home in NYC or Westchester, approved contractor, home must be service adequate. The discount comes off your contractor's invoice. A higher weatherized tier pays $10,000 ($11,000 in a disadvantaged community).

National Grid Clean Heat: full system
programs.rules: Upstate National Grid electric customer, participating contractor. Removing the old system raises it to $10,000 ($12,000 in a disadvantaged community).

programs.rules: Upstate National Grid electric customer, participating contractor.

programs.rules: RG&E electric customers, including the City of Rochester. Removing the old system raises it to $10,000.

programs.name: NYSEG Clean Heat: full system
programs.rules: NYSEG electric customers. Removing the old system raises it to $10,000 ($11,000 in a disadvantaged community).

programs.rules: Central Hudson electric customers, single-family home. Removing the old system raises it to $8,000. Apartments and homes under 1,000 sq ft get less.

programs.rules: Central Hudson electric customers, single-family home.

programs.name: Orange & Rockland Clean Heat: full system
programs.rules: O&R electric customers. Removing the old system raises it to $9,000 ($10,000 in a disadvantaged community).

programs.name: Orange & Rockland Clean Heat: partial system
PSEG Long Island heat pump rebate
programs.rules: Whole-home cold-climate heat pump on NEEP's list, sized for the whole home, with a participating contractor. Get pre-approval before work starts. Low-income households (under 60% of area median income) get $7,500, and moderate-income households get $5,000. PSEG Long Island is not part of NYS Clean Heat.

programs.name: NYS Clean Heat: heat pump water heater
programs.rules: Electric customers of the utility. Con Edison pays $1,000, the others $1,250.

programs.name: PSEG Long Island heat pump water heater
NYSERDA Comfort Home
programs.rules: Seal-and-insulate packages ($2,500 or $3,000, plus $2,000 for windows) through Comfort Home contractors in participating counties. Check that your county is covered. Not added to your total.

programs.name: NYSERDA EmPower+
programs.rules: Income-eligible owners and renters of 1-4 family homes. Low income: free upgrades up to $12,000 upstate or $14,000 downstate. Moderate income: 50% of cost up to $6,000 upstate or $7,000 downstate. Federal Home Energy Rebate money is delivered through EmPower+.

notes: Clean Heat incentives are capped at 70% of project cost (85% in a disadvantaged community).
New York has no general solar rebate for market-rate homes, and the federal solar credit ended for 2026 installs.
Amounts are for a single-family home. Apartments get about half. Your contractor confirms your tier.
